back: A settlement set up by a church to spread Christianity, usually with a church, a school and often a clinic.
A church founded by Africans that combines Christian faith with African forms of worship, prophecy and healing.

front: Who visited the Mutapa court in 1561?
back: Gonçalo da Silveira, a Portuguese Jesuit, who was killed the same year.

front: When and where did the LMS open a station in the Ndebele kingdom?
back: At Inyati in 1859, with the permission of King Mzilikazi.

front: Name four missions that came after the 1890s.
back: For example Jesuits, Methodists, Anglicans, Dutch Reformed, Salvation Army, Seventh-day Adventists, Brethren in Christ.

front: Name two Apostolic leaders from the 1930s.
Why is the link between missions and colonisation debated?
back: Missions brought education and health, but many missionaries came with the colonisers or accepted colonial rule and criticised African customs.

front: Why did Africans found their own churches?
back: To have leadership roles, African forms of worship and prayer for healing.
